summary.text: Cris Dush is a Republican member of the Pennsylvania Senate for the 25th District, which comprises Cameron, Clinton, Elk, McKean and Potter Counties and portions of Jefferson and Centre Counties.
He began his second term in January 2025 and chairs the Senate State Government Committee.

paragraphs.text: Dush is a native of Brookville, according to his official biography, and graduated from Brookville Area High School in 1979.
He attended Clarion State College before enlisting in the U.S. Air Force, where he held law enforcement and security positions.
In 1995 he returned to the Brookville area and spent 16 years with the Pennsylvania Department of Corrections, retiring as a corrections officer in January 2012.
In 2000, he enlisted with the 193rd Special Operations Wing of the Pennsylvania Air National Guard as a Security Forces member and was deployed in Operation Iraqi Freedom and Operation Noble Eagle.
He retired from the 193rd in December 2016 as a senior non-commissioned officer.

Before entering the Senate, Dush served six years in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives for the 66th Legislative District, which covers Jefferson County and municipalities in northern Indiana County.

For the 2025-26 session he is vice chair of the Intergovernmental Operations Committee and also serves on the Appropriations, Game and Fisheries, Judiciary, Local Government, and Veterans Affairs and Emergency Preparedness committees.

He was the first chairman of the PA Senate Second Amendment Caucus and the prime sponsor of Senate Bill 44, which became Act 39 of 2023, on services for sexually exploited child human trafficking victims.
He lives in Pine Creek Township, Jefferson County, with his wife, Traci.
